creative.basePrompt:
BRAND: Flickday Media — grassroots sports media company specializing in volleyball and action sports content. Chicago-based.
AESTHETIC: Sports press credential meets high-energy action photography. Think press badges, media passes, contact sheets, shutter speed displays, and field-side energy.

KEY VISUAL LANGUAGE:
- Camera aperture blades (6-blade iris) — the core brand motif
- Volleyball panel lines merged with aperture geometry
- Motion trails, speed lines, kinetic energy
- Press credential badges, lanyards, media passes
- Film strip frames, contact sheet grids
- Shutter speed / ISO / f-stop readouts as decorative type
- High contrast: yellow on black, or black on yellow
- Clean geometric shapes, no ornamental flourishes

constitution.brief: Resolve the Flickday Media identity: a wordmark that stands alone, a symbol that stands alone, and a lockup for the two together. The website, palette, and voice are already settled and stay. Only the marks are open.
constitution.conceptualAnchor: The flick — the decisive instant when action becomes a moment worth replaying.
nonGoals: Changing the palette or type system
Animating anything before the static mark works
Matching any legacy wordmark outline — systems A-D are forensic evidence of type drift, not geometry to preserve

Algorithmic kerning correction before finalists are chosen — equalising measured white area manufactures a preference and produced a k-d gap twice as tight as c-k in Sora. Native kerning until two or three finalists remain, then correct by eye
Letting a font being easy to fetch decide the identity — the first specimen pool was ten Google Fonts, mostly close relatives, which made the winner close to inevitable
priorApprovals: Yellow on near-black as the primary contrast pair (live site :root)
Tagline copy: Every Day's a Flickday (live site)
Anton as the site display face (live site :root)

Primary wordmark is clean lowercase lettering — no film reel or filmstrip substituted into the d. The play mark stays available as an independent secondary symbol or social bug, positioned adjacent to the wordmark, never nested inside it (nino, 2026-07-22)

No shipped Flickday wordmark outline is canonical. Continuity comes from the lowercase name, yellow-on-black, the voice, and the flick concept — not from legacy letterforms. Select the new typeface on brand fit, distinctiveness, production performance, and its ability to become one reproducible master (nino, 2026-07-22)
sources: apps/flickdaymedia/index.html — CANONICAL. Per BRAND-PRIORS.md, when a generated doc and the live site disagree, the site wins. That rule catches errors in BRAND-PRIORS itself.
Prior identity sessions — see decisions.rejections for what they ruled out

rubric.criterion: Reads as Flickday — authentic, energetic, player-first
Legible at favicon and watermark size
Wordmark and symbol each work alone
Sits correctly in the existing site header
Survives a circular social avatar crop
Holds as a CapCut watermark over footage
Reproduces in one color on apparel
Any aperture form has real blade count and rotation — check against a lens diagram, not a vibe
rubric.description: Lives here rather than in rejections: the brand's own icon is a ball-aperture, so a constraint matching the word would fire on every honest candidate. Mechanically wrong geometry is also not detectable from a descriptor — it needs eyes on the artifact.

rubric.criterion: Current without chasing a disposable trend
Becomes one reproducible master — a real typeface or true vector geometry that every variant is set from, not an outline nobody can regenerate

rejections.reason: An all-caps Bebas-class wordmark swap was tried and rejected; the lowercase logotype reads better
rejections.suggestion: Keep the logotype lowercase; the display face may still be all-caps for headlines

rejections.reason: Filmstrip forced into a letterform collapses at small sizes and reads as a rescue of an earlier artifact. Settled 2026-07-22: the construction is out, the motif is not — the play mark lives adjacent as its own symbol
rejections.suggestion: If the film metaphor earns its place, let it be the symbol — not a substituted glyph

rejections.reason: Symbol inserted into the word reduces readability of the name
rejections.suggestion: Keep the symbol adjacent, not substituted

rejections.reason: Typography changing between lockup variants means there is no system. Already happened: fingerprinting glyph outlines 2026-07-22 found at least three separate letterform systems across the shipped assets. System A (modular set) is Avenir Next Heavy converted to paths and IS regenerable via scripts/build-modular-wordmarks.mjs; systems B/C/D are potrace traces with no recoverable type identity. See apps/flickdaymedia/flickday-assets/wordmarks/existing-type-drift.png and concepts/2026-07-modular-wordmark/round-1/README.md
Multiple media metaphors stacked into one word never resolve

candidates.descriptor: The flick: the decisive instant when action becomes a moment worth replaying. One gesture of change, not an object — carries motion, wordmark, symbol and video behavior from a single idea.
The frame / the crop: what the photographer chooses to see, expressed as a bounding edge, corner marks or a viewfinder rectangle.
The ball and the flash: a volleyball combined with a burst or light source. Two literal objects, one from the sport and one from the camera, stacked into a single mark.
The F mark: a stylized letter F with built-in motion energy — a letterform execution rather than a strategic idea.
S-01 — Plus Jakarta Sans 800 lowercase logotype. Geometric sans, wide fit, tall x-height, neutral f and k.
S-02 — Baloo 2 800 lowercase logotype. Rounded terminals, chunky, friendly; softer than the incumbent.
S-03 — Manrope 800 lowercase logotype. Open counters, lighter apparent weight; thins at small size.
S-04 — Poppins 800 lowercase logotype. Geometric sans with near-circular bowls, wide, very heavy.
S-05 — Nunito 900 lowercase logotype. Rounded terminals, medium apparent weight, soft.
S-06 — Sora 800 lowercase logotype. Geometric sans, tight fit, round bowls, straight-tail y.
S-07 — Montserrat 800 lowercase logotype. Geometric sans, clean, slightly wide.
S-08 — Figtree 900 lowercase logotype. Geometric sans, dense, softly cut corners, tight fit.
S-09 — Fredoka 600 lowercase logotype. Rounded display face, least geometric of the set, lightest at small size.
S-10 — Rubik 800 lowercase logotype. Heavy geometric sans, wide, flat terminals, strongest at 11px.

ledger.rationale: The flick is native to the Flickday name. It connects sports and media without stacking volleyball and camera symbols, and it supports motion, wordmark, symbol and video behavior from one idea. Frame/crop is generic photography; ball + flash is overly literal; the F mark is an execution, not an idea.

The flick is native to the Flickday name. It connects sports and media without stacking volleyball and camera symbols, and it supports motion, wordmark, symbol and video behavior from one idea. Frame/crop is generic photography; ball + flash is overly literal; the F mark is an execution, not an idea.

Cut to three finalists, judged independently of any incumbent. Sora 800 leads: compact, decisive, contemporary, and able to carry sharper custom detail — it expresses the snap of the flick. Rubik 800 is the strongest challenger but its roundness reads friendlier and less sharp. Figtree 900 has the best utility and legibility and is the least distinctive. The seven cut here lose on brand fit, distinctiveness, or weight retention at small size.
